name: Rook
description: Point-trick family using the Rook deck: four colors (black, red, green, yellow), ranks 1–14 per color plus the Rook bird card. Popular in Mennonite communities and Eastern Kentucky. This entry models the common form: four in fixed partnerships, bid for nest and trump, first team to 500 wins.
deck: Rook 56-card deck (four colors 1–14 plus Rook bird card)

history.origins: Rook was introduced by Parker Brothers in 1906. The deck was designed for communities that avoided standard playing cards; the game became popular in Eastern Kentucky and among Mennonites in Southern Ontario, Manitoba, Pennsylvania, and Ohio.
timeline: 1906: Parker Brothers introduced the Rook deck and game; marketed to communities that avoided standard playing cards.

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships, partners opposite.
setup.deck: Rook deck: four suits (colors) 1–14 each plus Rook bird card. Common variant removes 2s, 3s, 4s for 45 cards.
setup.dealing: Ten cards each, one at a time; five cards to the nest. Dealer adds one card to the nest after each of the first five rounds of the deal.

rules.objective: As the bidding team, take at least the number of card points you bid; as the opposing team, score the points you take. First team to reach 500 or more points wins.
rules.gameplay: Four in fixed partnerships. Deal 10 each, 5 to nest. Bid from 100 in multiples of 5 (left of dealer first); three passes leave the fourth as high bidder; if first three pass, dealer must bid 100. Bidder picks up nest, discards five face-down (no point cards), names trump. Left of bidder leads; follow color; Rook is highest trump. Highest trump wins trick, else highest of led color. Bidder's team makes bid scores their points, else subtracts bid; other team always scores its points. Game to 500.
keyRules: 10 each, 5 to nest. Min bid 100, multiples of 5. Bidder takes nest, discards 5 (no point cards), names trump. Follow color; Rook highest trump. 180 points per deal. First to 500 wins.

strategy.basic: Bid when you have good trump and point cards; avoid overbidding.
strategy.intermediate: Count trumps and key cards; adjust bidding and play.
strategy.advanced: Partnership signaling and endplay; near-optimal bidding and defense.
tips: Bidder may not put point cards in the nest.
If first three pass, dealer must bid 100.

scoring.description: Card points: 1=15, 14=10, 10=10, 5=5, Rook=20 (180 per deal). Bidder's team scores its points if they make the bid, else subtracts the bid; other team always scores its points. First team to 500 wins.
scoring.winCondition: First team to 500 or more; higher score wins.
